items.title: The Gorenstein locus of a flat locally finite type morphism commutes with arbitrary base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a flat locally finite type morphism f : X -> Y, the lemma asserts that the formation of the set of points x where f is Gorenstein commutes with arbitrary base change (statement lines 6682-6688). The proof notes that the assumption makes every fibre locally finite type over a field, hence locally Noetherian, and the same holds after base change, so the statement makes sense; looking at fibres it reduces to the problem that for X locally of finite type over a field k, a field extension K/k and a point x_K of X_K over x, the local ring O_{X_K,x_K} is Gorenstein if and only if O_{X,x} is (proof lines 6690-6703). The problem is then solved algebraically: the proof chooses an affine open Spec(A) containing x corresponding to a prime p, sets A_K = A otimes_k K so that Spec(A_K) contains x_K corresponding to a prime p_K, and takes a dualizing complex omega_A^bullet for A, for which omega_A^bullet otimes_A A_K is a dualizing complex for A_K by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-base-change-dualizing-over-field (proof lines 6705-6714). The conclusion follows because A_p -> (A_K)_{p_K} is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian rings, so (omega_A^bullet)_p is invertible over D(A_p) if and only if its base change is invertible over D((A_K)_{p_K}); the author marks the last step 'Some details omitted; hint: look at cohomology modules' (proof lines 6716-6719). Reducing to the fibre over a field extension and then to invertibility of the localised dualizing complex along a flat local homomorphism is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
